text:
maya: Opening a docs PR to refresh the Starter Kit quickstart — focus is on clarifying auth and the "first deploy" path. PR: http://git.internal/r/redwood/docs/pull/4122. Main changes: use REDWOOD_API_KEY env var consistently, provide a minimal curl + JS + Python snippet, remove old 'publish' step, and add a short note about Dedicated vs Hosted picks. Requesting reviews from eng-runtime and devex.

docs-bot: PR #4122 created by maya — CI checks queued (:hourglass:).

alice: Thanks — quick question: can we add a short paragraph about using KMS/HSM for managed keys vs local env var for tests? Compliance folks ask for this phrasing.

jon: I'll take the JS snippets. Can you split the SDK example into "minimal" and "production" variants? Minimal should show one request + env var, production should show batching hint and error handling.

maya: Yep, good call. I'll split them and keep the minimal one very compact. Also saw a broken anchor link to the auth section in quickstart — that's failing markdown-lint. I'll fix it in this PR.

sam: FYI the sample Dockerfile in starter-repo fails on node 20 because of native deps. Options: pin to node:18, or bump deps to prebuilt binaries. I prefer pin for now.

chris: I can open a small patch to pin node in the Dockerfile and reference it from the PR if you want.

jon: Also, the import path in the JS example needs to match the new SDK surface — update from `@redwood/sdk` -> `@redwood/inference-js` (we pushed that change last week). I'll add a comment in the PR review.

docs-bot: markdown-lint error in docs/quickstart/hello.md: line 42 — bad-link (anchor not found).

maya: Fixed the anchor in the doc and pushed a commit. Also added a short note under "auth" showing `export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<token>"` and a one-liner curl example:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-4-mini","input":"hello world"}'
```

alice: Nice — can you add the KMS sentence under the same section like: "For production, you should use a secrets manager / KMS and inject the key at runtime (see internal KMS guide)" — keep it short.

jon: Left a few inline nits: code fence language on the Python example, and a missing async/await in the JS streaming snippet. Tiny changes, should be quick.

sam: I added a tiny test to the starter app repo to assert the env var path exists during local runs — added as a separate PR and referenced it.

chris: Dockerfile pin PR is #4123 — I linked it in the PR description and added a note: "pin node 18 until deps updated".

maya: Pushed revisions that address the linting and most comments. Requesting reviews: @alice @jon @sam. I've also added a changelog line under "Quickstart: clarify auth + first deploy" for release notes.

docs-bot: CI run completed — markdown-lint now passes, but docs-ci flagged a preview link build warning (image alt text missing) — see artifact.

deploy-bot: Staging preview published: https://staging-docs.redwood.ai/preview/4122 (use this to sanity-check the snippets).

alice: Reviewing the content now, will post comments by EOD. :thumbsup:

jon: Reviewed and approved with minor nit fixes — suggest we squash the tiny formatting commits.

sam: Approved from sample-app side; tests green.

chris: Docker PR #4123 merged.

maya: Thanks all — planning to merge once alice approves and the preview looks good. I'll open a follow-up issue to update the starter repo README with explicit local dev token steps and link to the KMS guide.

docs-bot: PR #4122 merged by maya (:rocket:).

deploy-bot: Prod docs updated — live at https://docs.redwood.ai/quickstart/hello.

jon: Great work, nice and compact now.

alice: Small follow-up: can we add a single-sentence troubleshooting tip about 401 vs 403 errors? I'll add it in a follow-up PR.

maya: Will do — opening follow-up PR after this lands. Thanks everyone! :sparkles:
